messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 - Hosted API p95/p99 token latency spike + queue growth in us-west. Auto-scale attempts failing. @mike.k @sophia.r paging now.

mike.k: seeing queue length jump on ingress queues -> ~180k pending across gpu pools, p95 1.2s -> 4.8s, p99 2.4s -> 12s, error rate up from 0.2% to 3.5%. Customers see timeouts.

sophia.r: confirmed. autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts that time out during instance creation; cloud API 429 on instance-create. Provisioner stuck in RetryBackoff.

arya.p: adding some quick context: we have thin-provisioned pools in us-west-2 for hosted; burst config set to 20% over reserved. Looks like we hit cloud quota + regional provisioning slowness.

jordan.s: can we route low-priority traffic to model-fallback tier? That will reduce GPU pressure while we fix provisioning.

mike.k: yes, initiating soft-throttle route to fallback-quantized (lower-cost) for non-SRE customer tags. Doing gradual 25% -> 50% rollout.

infra-bot: deploy triggered: route:update --from=hosted-prod --to=fallback-quantized --selector="priority:low" --pct=25

ops-lead: @sophia.r handoff in 15min if not resolved. Note: PG tonight has high critical workloads. Keep me posted.

sophia.r: Ran a quick check on autoscaler: terraform-provisioner stuck on create-vm step. Cloud error snippet: 
```
ERROR: QuotaExceeded: Insufficient vCPUs in region us-west-2 for requested shape
RequestID: abc123-create-2026
```

sophia.r: Also seeing API 429s in the create path. There are several retries buffered; autoscaler backoff doubled each attempt.

arya.p: OK doing two immediate things: (1) manual warm-up of ephemeral GPU nodes from spare dedicated pool (if infra approves), (2) escalate quota increase with cloud support.

mike.k: infra slacked approval request to infra on-call. pinging @infra oncall.

infra-bot: oncall: @jordan.s assigned (pager).

jordan.s: acknowledged. I'll check reserved pools and evictions. If we can temporarily borrow 8x a100 from the Internal Dedicated pool, we can drain backlog and buy time.

jordan.s: quick command to list pool utilization: 
```
redwoodctl pool list --region us-west-2 --type gpu --json | jq '.pools[] | {name,used,capacity}'
```

mike.k: output shows dedicated-internal has 12/20 used; we can spare 6. Would prefer internal ops signoff.

ops-lead: approved temporary reassign of 6 nodes with tags "emergency-borrow". Make sure billing signals are captured.

jordan.s: reassigning 6 nodes to hosted-prod using pool-api: 
```
pool-api assign --pool dedicated-internal --target hosted-prod --count 6 --tags emergency-borrow
```

infra-bot: pool assignment accepted, starting reconfigure. Expected 3-4m until nodes appear in autoscaler pool.

sophia.r: in the meantime I'm expanding the fallback routing to 50% for low-priority and enabling request-level caching for repeated prefixes from top customers (quick win).

mike.k: adding temporary throttle rule for bulk inference routes to cap RPS per-customer to 60% of baseline. This should protect control-plane and reduce queue growth.

incident-bot: metric snapshot: 
- queue_length_total: 180k -> 90k after routing change and pool assign started
- p95 latency: 4.8s -> 2.1s
- p99 latency: 12s -> 6.5s
- errors: 3.5% -> 1.1%

arya.p: cloud support case opened (CS-87321) requesting quota bump and expedited review. Case link: https://cloud.example/cases/CS-87321 (internal).

sophia.r: autoscaler logs after pool assign: some create requests still erroring but new nodes from borrowed pool registered successfully. We have immediate capacity for ~18k extra concurrent tokens. Backlog draining slowly.

mike.k: starting retrospective notes for customer impact: some customers experienced increased latency and client retries; a subset of streaming connections dropped due to per-conn timeouts (30s). We've flagged top 5 impacted customers for outreach.

jordan.s: doing a running-check on eviction churn: no major evictions observed during borrow. Eviction wait time reduced from ~120s -> 28s now that warm nodes came online.

ops-lead: @mike.k prepare a post-incident email draft for CSMs with timeline + mitigation + next steps. Include compensation guidance if needed.

mike.k: drafting now. Key timeline:
- 3755555555 incident-bot alert -> autoscale failed on quota
- 3755555620 routing rollback -> launched fallback-quantized at 25%
- 3755555655 increased fallback to 50% + throttle rules
- 3755555687 pool borrow 6 nodes assigned -> nodes online by 3755555725
- 3755555783 backlog drained to <5k pending

sophia.r: action items for postmortem:
- add autoscaler retry budget and circuit-breaker for create-vm path
- add quota-check preflight so autoscaler will fail fast with clear err msg and trigger alternate flows earlier
- implement cross-pool borrowing runbook (docs + infra approvals)
- add synthetic tests to surface provisioning throttles earlier in canary windows

infra-bot: ticket created: INFRA-3421 "enable temporary pool-borrow workflow + audit logging".

arya.p: any customer-facing outage label? I'd mark this as "degraded" with partial request failures/timeouts for ~35 minutes (start->drain).

mike.k: agreed. tagging incident SEV2, scoped impact to hosted-prod us-west-2, timeframe ~3755555555 -> 3755555783.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident moved to mitigation state. Oncall handoff scheduled to @sophia.r at +15m if not resolved.

jordan.s: I'll follow up with infra to chase the quota bump. If cloud can't provide quota quickly, we should bake automated fallback to allocate from dedicated pools earlier.

mike.k: thanks all. I'll finish customer comms and notify CSMs. Leaving thread open for postmortem notes.

sophia.r: note for postmortem: include metric graphs (ingress qlen, instance-create errors, p95/p99 latency) and exact autoscaler log snippets.

ops-lead: great job triaging fast. We'll close when postmortem and action items have owners.

incident-bot: paging cleared for primary oncall. Archive when done. :spiral_note_pad:"
